objective: Review the non-executing native-parser adapter-payload to sidecar plan-resolution handoff-contract metadata fixture and accept only ready-only metadata construction, while keeping command synthesis, operator-plan production, runtime handoff execution, RTL execution, compare execution, measurement, timing, runtime/ABI, arbitrary RTL/filelist support, automatic allocation, upstream regression success, and upstream landing claims out of scope.

review_decision.reason: The implementation now matches the reviewed ready-only metadata boundary: the public plan-resolution module only exposes a thin wrapper, the support module validates the ready plan-resolution surface before calling sidecar_handoff_contract, not-ready and unsupported results return structured closed metadata without handoff_contract, and malformed ready inputs fail before the metadata authority can read stage details.
review_decision.weakest_point: The term sidecar_handoff_contract can still be over-read as sidecar runtime handoff validation, command readiness, or coverage-output evidence. The implementation is accepted only because it produces metadata, blocks command synthesis, operator plan, execution, measurement, timing, runtime/ABI changes, source-closure inference, filelist expansion, automatic allocation, and now also rejects efficiency_estimate_invoked before metadata construction.

accepted_blocker_fix.issue: ready handoff validation did not originally check efficiency_estimate_invoked
accepted_blocker_fix.required_check: efficiency_estimate_invoked is false before sidecar_handoff_contract can be called

required_next_gate.name: define_verilator_native_option_parser_sidecar_plan_resolution_handoff_contract_operator_plan_boundary_gate

whether command argv, estimate command, and operator plan are still non-executing planning outputs
which fields remain sidecar-owned and may not be inferred from parser-preserved source files or filelists
the rejection behavior for closed, unsupported, malformed, or prepopulated handoff-contract metadata
tests that prove command/operator-plan production remains separate from RTL execution, compare execution, timing, runtime/ABI changes, arbitrary filelist expansion, and automatic allocation

non_claims: not a native Verilator parser implementation
not operator-plan production from native parser payload
not coverage-output equivalence for a native-parser flow
not a new public CLI or workflow
not automatic optimal GPU allocation for any design
not a runtime or ABI change
not GEM benchmark or comparison evidence
